objects.definition:
enum pcmk_sim_flags {
    pcmk_sim_none             = 0,
    pcmk_sim_all_actions      = UINT32_C(1) << 0,
    pcmk_sim_show_pending     = UINT32_C(1) << 1,
    pcmk_sim_process          = UINT32_C(1) << 2,
    pcmk_sim_show_scores      = UINT32_C(1) << 3,
    pcmk_sim_show_utilization = UINT32_C(1) << 4,
    pcmk_sim_simulate         = UINT32_C(1) << 5,
    pcmk_sim_sanitized        = UINT32_C(1) << 6,
    pcmk_sim_verbose          = UINT32_C(1) << 7,
};
objects.description: Bitmask flags controlling behavior and verbosity of cluster simulation routines (e.g., pcmk_simulate). Values are individual bits suitable for OR-combination.

Container of synthetic cluster events to inject for simulations: node state changes, operation injections/failures, ticket state changes, and cluster-wide booleans for watchdog/quorum. Lists hold gchar* entries; strings are owned by the structure until freed.
Bitmask flags selecting which fields (numeric code, name, description) to display for result codes when using APIs like pcmk_show_result_code and pcmk_list_result_codes.

Inline helper function that clamps an integer log level into the 0..UINT8_MAX range. Although it is a function, no custom struct/enum/typedef types are defined in this header; included here to note that there are no user-defined types introduced. No pointer type applicable beyond the return type form.

Forward-declared/external type from libqb used throughout macros and function prototypes here (e.g., crm_is_callsite_active). It is referenced but not defined in this header, so it should be ignored per instructions. Included here only to acknowledge absence of custom type definitions.
Connection state of the fencer (STONITH) API. Deprecated external API indicator of whether the client is connected for commands, queries, or disconnected.

objects.description: Bitmask flags influencing behavior of API requests (sync vs async, self-fencing allowance, history cleanup/broadcast, etc.). Deprecated.
State progression of a fencing operation (query, execute, done, duplicate, failed). Order matters. Deprecated.
Fence agent interface families supported by Pacemaker: internal, RHCS, LHA, or any/invalid. Deprecated.
Singly linked list node of key/value string pairs, used for agent parameters and device lists. Deprecated. Caller typically manages with helper functions to add/free nodes.
Linked-list entry describing a completed fencing action: target, action, originator, delegate, client, state, completion time (sec + nsec), and exit reason. Deprecated.

objects.definition: typedef struct stonith_s stonith_t;
objects.description: Opaque handle type for a fencer API connection. The concrete struct is defined later in this header; users typically treat it opaquely. Deprecated for external use.
Notification payload for fence-related events and results: identifiers, action, target, result code, device, and an opaque pointer for internal use. Deprecated.
Data delivered to async result callbacks: return code, call id, user data, and an internal opaque pointer. Deprecated.

Vtable of function pointers that implement the legacy STONITH client API: connection management, device/level registration, queries, actions, callbacks, and validation. Deprecated; replaced by libpacemaker functions.
Concrete fencer API connection object holding state, last call id, private implementation pointer, and the operations vtable. Deprecated for external use.

objects.definition: typedef int (*st_api_kick_fn) (int nodeid, const char *uname, int timeout, bool off);
objects.description: Function pointer type to the dynamically loaded symbol stonith_api_kick in libstonithd; requests fencing a node. Used by helper to avoid link-time dependency.

objects.definition: typedef time_t (*st_api_time_fn) (int nodeid, const char *uname, bool in_progress);
objects.description: Function pointer type to the dynamically loaded symbol stonith_api_time in libstonithd; queries last fence time or in-progress status for a node. Used by helper to avoid link-time dependency.
Enumeration of LSB-compliant exit codes for generic actions. Used to normalize results from service operations to well-known LSB values.
Enumeration of LSB status action exit codes. Distinct from generic action exit codes; used for status queries.
Bitmask flags that modify how a service action is executed (process group handling, blocking behavior).

objects.definition: typedef struct svc_action_private_s svc_action_private_t;
objects.description: Opaque internal type holding implementation-specific state for svc_action_t. Not defined in this header; contents are private to the library.

Primary object representing an external action execution (resource agent, alert agent, or generic command). Contains identity, parameters, execution control and results, plus internal state. Should be created via API functions and freed with services_action_free().

functions.name: pcmk_controller_status
functions.signature: int pcmk_controller_status(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *node_name, unsigned int message_timeout_ms);
functions.description: Get controller (pacemaker-controld) status for the designated node (or the DC if node_name is NULL) and place the result into an XML tree. The IPC dispatch mode depends on message_timeout_ms (0 => sync, otherwise poll). Use to query live controller status for tooling or diagnostics.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable where the result tree will be stored
node_name may be NULL to query the designated controller (DC)
message_timeout_ms controls wait behavior: 0 uses pcmk_ipc_dispatch_sync; nonzero uses pcmk_ipc_dispatch_poll
Caller should check the returned standard Pacemaker return code before using the XML result

functions.name: pcmk_designated_controller
functions.description: Query and output the designated controller (DC) node name into an XML tree. The IPC dispatch mode is chosen based on message_timeout_ms as with other controller queries.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
message_timeout_ms of 0 uses pcmk_ipc_dispatch_sync; otherwise pcmk_ipc_dispatch_poll
Caller must check the standard Pacemaker return code before using the result

functions.name: pcmk_free_injections
functions.description: Free a pcmk_injections_t structure and its allocated members. Use after finishing with an injections bundle used for simulations.
requirements: injections may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a pcmk_injections_t previously allocated/initialized for use
After this call, injections and any contained pointers must not be accessed

functions.name: pcmk_query_node_info
functions.signature: int pcmk_query_node_info(xmlNodePtr *xml, uint32_t *node_id, char **node_name, char **uuid, char **state, bool *have_quorum, bool *is_remote, bool show_output, unsigned int message_timeout_ms);
functions.description: Query the controller for node information (name, UUID, membership state, quorum, remote status) corresponding to a node ID and optionally output it to an XML tree. If node_id is NULL or 0, the local node is queried; on success, the true node ID is stored back via node_id when provided. The function can also emit formatted node info when show_output is true.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
node_id may be NULL; if non-NULL and contains 0, the local node is queried; on success the true node ID is stored back
node_name, uuid, and state are optional; if non-NULL and the call succeeds, the caller is responsible for freeing *node_name, *uuid, and *state using free()
have_quorum and is_remote are optional output booleans; pass non-NULL to receive values
show_output controls whether node info is emitted
message_timeout_ms of 0 uses pcmk_ipc_dispatch_sync; otherwise pcmk_ipc_dispatch_poll
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker return code before using outputs

functions.name: pcmk_query_node_name
functions.signature: static inline int pcmk_query_node_name(xmlNodePtr *xml, uint32_t node_id, char **node_name, unsigned int message_timeout_ms);
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper around pcmk_query_node_info to fetch only the node name for a given node ID (or 0 for the local node). It suppresses additional fields and output.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
node_id may be 0 to query the local node
node_name must be non-NULL if the caller expects a name; on success the caller must free *node_name with free()
message_timeout_ms of 0 uses pcmk_ipc_dispatch_sync; otherwise pcmk_ipc_dispatch_poll
Return value is a standard Pacemaker return code and must be checked

functions.name: pcmk_pacemakerd_status
functions.signature: int pcmk_pacemakerd_status(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *ipc_name, unsigned int message_timeout_ms);
functions.description: Query and output pacemakerd status via its IPC service, writing the result into an XML tree. Dispatch mode is determined by message_timeout_ms as documented.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ipc_name must be a valid pacemakerd IPC name string
message_timeout_ms of 0 uses pcmk_ipc_dispatch_sync; otherwise pcmk_ipc_dispatch_poll
Caller must check the standard Pacemaker return code before using the result

functions.name: pcmk_resource_delete
functions.signature: int pcmk_resource_delete(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *rsc_id, const char *rsc_type);
functions.description: Remove a resource (primitive, group, etc.) by ID from the configuration, writing result details to XML. Deleting something that does not exist is treated as success.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
rsc_id must identify the resource to remove
rsc_type should describe the resource type (e.g., "primitive", "group"); mismatches are tolerated and treated as success
Caller must check the standard Pacemaker return code

functions.name: pcmk_resource_digests
functions.signature: int pcmk_resource_digests(xmlNodePtr *xml, pcmk_resource_t *rsc, const pcmk_node_t *node, GHashTable *overrides);
functions.description: Compute and output the operation parameter digests for a resource on a given node, optionally applying configuration overrides. The results are written to XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
rsc must point to a valid scheduler resource object
node must point to the target node whose history/parameters are relevant
overrides may be NULL or a hash table of config parameter overrides
Caller must check the standard Pacemaker return code

functions.name: pcmk_simulate
functions.signature: int pcmk_simulate(xmlNodePtr *xml, pcmk_scheduler_t *scheduler, const pcmk_injections_t *injections, unsigned int flags, unsigned int section_opts, const char *use_date, const char *input_file, const char *graph_file, const char *dot_file);
functions.description: Run a high-level cluster simulation (akin to crm_simulate), applying synthetic events (nodes up/down, tickets, injected ops) to an input CIB and producing artifacts such as a transition graph and/or dot output. Writes overall results/status to XML. Behavior is modified by flags and section_opts; the CIB input file may be overwritten.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
scheduler must be an initialized pcmk_scheduler_t context
injections may be NULL or must point to a pcmk_injections_t describing events
flags is a bitmask of enum pcmk_sim_flags
section_opts selects which status sections are displayed
use_date may be NULL or a date string to set the simulated cluster time
input_file may be NULL; when non-NULL it may be overwritten by this function
graph_file and dot_file may be NULL; when non-NULL the function will write the corresponding artifacts
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code before using outputs

functions.name: pcmk_verify
functions.description: Verify a CIB for errors/warnings (akin to crm_verify) and write XML-formatted output. The CIB can be sourced from the live cluster, stdin, a string beginning with '<', or a filename.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
cib_source interpretation: NULL -> use live CIB; "-" -> stdin; string starting with '<' -> XML string; otherwise -> file path
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_nodes
functions.description: List nodes, optionally filtered by type(s), and write the list as XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
node_types may be NULL or a string indicating which node types to include (default: all)
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_status
functions.description: Output cluster status formatted like `crm_mon --output-as=xml`, writing into an XML tree.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_check_rules
functions.signature: int pcmk_check_rules(xmlNodePtr *xml, xmlNodePtr input, const crm_time_t *date, const char **rule_ids);
functions.description: Evaluate whether each rule identified in a NULL-terminated list is in effect against the provided or live CIB at a given date/time, emitting results to XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
input may be NULL to use the current CIB; otherwise must be CIB XML
date may be NULL to use the current date/time; otherwise must point to a valid crm_time_t
rule_ids must be a NULL-terminated list of rule ID strings
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_check_rule
functions.signature: static inline int pcmk_check_rule(xmlNodePtr *xml, xmlNodePtr input, const crm_time_t *date, const char *rule_id);
functions.description: Convenience inline wrapper around pcmk_check_rules to check a single rule by ID at a given date/time against the provided or live CIB, writing results to XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
input may be NULL to use the current CIB; otherwise must be CIB XML
date may be NULL to use the current date/time; otherwise must be a valid crm_time_t pointer
rule_id must be a valid rule identifier string
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_show_result_code
functions.signature: int pcmk_show_result_code(xmlNodePtr *xml, int code, enum pcmk_result_type type, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Display the numeric code, name, and/or description for a result code of the specified family, writing the formatted info to XML. Output fields are controlled by pcmk_rc_disp_flags.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
code is the result code value to describe
type selects the result code family (supported: pcmk_result_legacy, pcmk_result_rc, pcmk_result_exitcode)
flags is a bitmask of pcmk_rc_disp_flags controlling which fields are displayed
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_result_codes
functions.signature: int pcmk_list_result_codes(xmlNodePtr *xml, enum pcmk_result_type type, uint32_t flags);
functions.description: List all valid result codes in a given result-code family and write their information to XML. Output fields are controlled by pcmk_rc_disp_flags.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
type selects the result code family (supported: pcmk_result_legacy, pcmk_result_rc, pcmk_result_exitcode)
flags is a bitmask of pcmk_rc_disp_flags controlling which fields are displayed
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_alternatives
functions.description: List available providers for the given OCF resource agent and output as XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
agent_spec must be the resource agent name
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_agents
functions.description: List all agents available for a specified standard and/or provider (format: STD[:PROV]) and write as XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
agent_spec must be a string of the form STD or STD:PROV
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_providers
functions.description: List all available OCF providers for the specified agent and write as XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
agent_spec must be the resource agent name
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_standards
functions.description: List all available resource agent standards and write as XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_cluster_options
functions.description: List cluster-wide options (including advanced/deprecated when all is true) as XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNode* variable (xmlNode**) for the result tree
all controls inclusion of advanced/deprecated options (currently always treated as true)
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_fencing_params
functions.description: List common Pacemaker-processed fencing resource parameters (not agent/library params) as XML. The all flag controls inclusion of advanced/deprecated options.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNode* variable (xmlNode**) for the result tree
all controls inclusion of advanced/deprecated options (currently always treated as true)
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_list_primitive_meta
functions.description: List meta-attributes applicable to primitive resources as OCF-like XML. For XML output, the 'all' flag is always treated as true.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNode* variable (xmlNode**) for the result tree
all is accepted but for XML output objects is always treated as true
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_constraints
functions.description: Return constraints that apply to a given ticket (or all ticket constraints if ticket_id is NULL), writing results to XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id may be NULL to list all ticket constraints
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_delete
functions.signature: int pcmk_ticket_delete(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *ticket_id, bool force);
functions.description: Delete a ticket's state from the local cluster site, writing result to XML. If the ticket is granted, deletion requires force=true.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id must identify the ticket to delete
If the ticket has been granted, force must be true to proceed; otherwise the call fails (EACCES)
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_get_attr
functions.signature: int pcmk_ticket_get_attr(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *ticket_id, const char *attr_name, const char *attr_default);
functions.description: Get the value of an attribute on a ticket, writing the value to XML. If the ticket or attribute does not exist, attr_default is used as the value in the output.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id must identify the ticket
attr_name must be the attribute name to fetch
attr_default may be NULL; used when either the ticket or attribute does not exist
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_info
functions.description: Return information about a ticket (or all tickets if ticket_id is NULL), writing details to XML.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id may be NULL to report all tickets
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_remove_attr
functions.signature: int pcmk_ticket_remove_attr(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *ticket_id, GList *attr_delete, bool force);
functions.description: Remove one or more attributes from a ticket, writing results to XML. Attempting to remove the granted attribute fails with EACCES unless force is true.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id must identify the ticket
attr_delete must be a list of attribute names (GList of char*) to remove
If removing the granted attribute, force must be true; otherwise the call fails with EACCES
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_set_attr
functions.signature: int pcmk_ticket_set_attr(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *ticket_id, GHashTable *attr_set, bool force);
functions.description: Set attributes on a ticket, writing results to XML. Changing the granted status requires force=true. If the ticket does not exist and attr_set is non-NULL, it is created with the given attributes.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id must identify the ticket to modify or create
attr_set may be NULL or a hash of attribute names to values
Changing the granted attribute requires force=true; otherwise the call fails with EACCES
If ticket_id does not exist and attr_set is non-NULL, the ticket will be created
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_ticket_state
functions.description: Return the state XML for a ticket (or all tickets if ticket_id is NULL), writing results to XML. If multiple tickets exist with the same non-NULL ID, returns pcmk_rc_duplicate_id.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
ticket_id may be NULL to fetch state for all tickets
If ticket_id is not NULL and duplicates exist, the function returns pcmk_rc_duplicate_id
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_request_fencing
functions.signature: int pcmk_request_fencing(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *target, const char *action, const char *name, unsigned int timeout, unsigned int tolerance, int delay, char **reason);
functions.description: Request that the cluster perform a fencing action (on/off/reboot) against a target node, waiting up to timeout and writing results to XML. If a successful action for the target occurred within the specified tolerance window, return success without performing the action again. An optional delay can be applied; a delay of -1 applies no delay and disables any configured fencing delay. On failure, a descriptive reason can be returned.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree
target must be the node to fence (by name or ID per cluster conventions)
action must be a fencing action string such as "on", "off", or "reboot"
name should identify the requester
timeout is in milliseconds and limits how long to wait for completion
tolerance is in milliseconds; if a matching successful action occurred within this window, the function returns success without re-fencing
delay is in milliseconds; -1 means no delay and disables any pcmk_delay_base/pcmk_delay_max fencing delays
reason may be non-NULL; on return and failure it may be set to an allocated descriptive string that the caller must free
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_history
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_history(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *target, unsigned int timeout, bool quiet, int verbose, bool broadcast, bool cleanup);
functions.description: List fencing operations that have occurred for a specific node, optionally aggregating from all nodes and/or cleaning up history, writing results to XML. If xml is not NULL, any previous XML tree will be freed and replaced.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
target must be the node whose fence history to retrieve
timeout is in milliseconds for the operation
quiet suppresses most output; verbose includes additional output detail
broadcast, when true, gathers fencing history from all nodes
cleanup, when true, cleans up fencing history after listing
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_installed
functions.description: List all installed fence agents and write them as XML. If xml is not NULL, any previous contents will be freed first. The timeout parameter is currently ignored.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
timeout is accepted but ignored
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_last
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_last(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *target, bool as_nodeid);
functions.description: Report when a device (node) was last fenced, writing results to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed. The target can be given as a node ID when as_nodeid is true.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
target must identify the node that was fenced
as_nodeid indicates target is a node ID when true, otherwise a node name
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_list_targets
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_list_targets(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *device_id, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: List nodes that can be fenced by a specific fence device, writing results to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
device_id must be the resource ID of the fence device
timeout is in milliseconds for the operation
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_metadata
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_metadata(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *agent, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: Retrieve metadata for a fence agent and write it to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
agent must be the fence agent name to query
timeout is in milliseconds for the operation
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_registered
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_registered(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *target, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: List registered fence devices, optionally restricted to those that can fence the specified target, writing results to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
target may be NULL to list all devices or a node identifier to filter devices capable of fencing it
timeout is in milliseconds for the operation
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_register_level
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_register_level(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *target, int fence_level, GList *devices);
functions.description: Register a fencing topology level mapping a target selector to a list of devices, writing results to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed. Target selection supports name=value (attribute), @pattern (node name pattern), or a node name.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
target must specify the selection ("name=value", "@pattern", or a node name)
fence_level is the index number of the level to add
devices must be a GList of char* device IDs to use in the level
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_unregister_level
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_unregister_level(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *target, int fence_level);
functions.description: Unregister a fencing topology level for a given target selector and level index, writing results to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
target must specify the selection ("name=value", "@pattern", or a node name)
fence_level is the index number of the level to remove
Caller must check the returned standard Pacemaker code

functions.name: pcmk_fence_validate
functions.signature: int pcmk_fence_validate(xmlNodePtr *xml, const char *agent, const char *id, GHashTable *params, unsigned int timeout);
functions.description: Validate a fence device configuration for a given agent, device ID, and parameters, writing validation results to XML. If xml is not NULL, previous contents will be freed.
requirements: xml must be a valid pointer to an xmlNodePtr variable for the result tree; if not NULL, previous contents will be freed and lost
agent must be the fence agent name (e.g., "fence_xvm")
id may be NULL or the fence device ID
params must be a hash table of configuration parameters expected by the agent

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target fuzzers use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for various strings (entity names and argv entries).
# Data type: free-form string. We should return a single bytes buffer that the harness
# will split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumptions. Typical fuzz engines (e.g.,
# libFuzzer-style) often draw successive strings from the same input by length-prefixing
# or delimiter-based parsing. Since we can’t control the harness, we aim to provide a
# compact buffer containing multiple plausible, varied, null-terminated C-strings, which
# frequently works for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers in these fuzz setups.
#
# Goals for interesting, yet valid inputs for the provided stubs (crm_log_preinit, crm_log_init):
# - Mix of empty, short, long (<=256) strings.
# - Include typical program names, options (-V, --verbose, -q, --quiet, --daemon), paths,
#   and unusual characters/spaces.
# - Provide NULL-terminated segments so C string reads are safe.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a sequence of C-strings joined together, each null-terminated. The harness can
#   consume them in order for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# - Include some duplicated and variant arguments to exercise different code paths.
# - Randomize ordering/content with the given seed for variability while staying valid.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_ARG_LEN = 256  # stub truncates to 256, keep within

_COMMON_ENTITIES = [
    "pacemakerd", "crmd", "stonithd", "pengine", "lrmd", "attrd",
    "pcmk-test", "cluster-sim", "monitor", "logger"
]

_COMMON_ARGS = [
    "-V", "-VV", "-VVV", "--verbose", "--quiet", "-q", "--daemon",
    "--no-daemon", "--log-to-stderr", "--no-stderr", "--blackbox",
    "--color=always", "--color=never", "--trace", "--debug",
]

_PATHS = [
    "/usr/sbin/pacemakerd", "/usr/libexec/pacemaker/controld",
    "/sbin/stonithd", "/bin/true", "/bin/echo", "/tmp/test\nname",
]

_WEIRD = [
    "", " ", "\t", "--=--", "name with spaces", "unicodé",
    "A" * 64, "B" * 128, "C" * 255,
]

# Some environment-like key=val pairs useful as argv entries
_ENVLIKE = [
    "PCMK_logfile=/var/log/pacemaker.log",
    "PCMK_debug=1", "PCMK_trace_files=all", "PCMK_stderr=1",
    "PCMK_service=ocf", "LC_ALL=C", "LANG=C.UTF-8",
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(len(items))]

def _gen_entity(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes empty (to simulate NULL path in fuzzer choosing nullptr), sometimes name
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return ""
    base = _rand_choice(rng, _COMMON_ENTITIES)
    # Occasionally add suffix/prefix
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base = base + str(rng.randint(0, 9))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        base = "org.pacemaker." + base
    return base[:MAX_ARG_LEN]

def _gen_arg(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.35:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, _COMMON_ARGS)
    elif roll < 0.6:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, _ENVLIKE)
    elif roll < 0.8:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, _PATHS)
    elif roll < 0.9:
        # random short token
        length = rng.randint(1, 20)
        alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_:."
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    else:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, _WEIRD)
    return s[:MAX_ARG_LEN]

def _null_term(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure valid UTF-8 bytes; fallback replace to keep bytes valid; FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # typically treats as bytes up to NUL.
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'replace') + b"\x00"

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Provide multiple entities first to satisfy several FUZZ_PARAM_STR pulls
    # across both stubs
    entity_count = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(entity_count):
        parts.append(_null_term(_gen_entity(rng)))

    # Provide a cluster of argv-style entries (the stubs may read up to 16 args)
    argc = rng.randint(0, 16)
    for _ in range(argc):
        parts.append(_null_term(_gen_arg(rng)))

    # Add some extras to ensure future FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls still have material
    extra = rng.randint(4, 12)
    for _ in range(extra):
        parts.append(_null_term(_gen_arg(rng)))

    # Ensure total size is bounded
    buf = b"".join(parts)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure we end with a NUL so last string is properly terminated
        if not buf.endswith(b"\x00"):
            # Replace last byte with NUL to avoid exceeding limit
            buf = buf[:-1] + b"\x00"

    # Guarantee non-empty buffer and at least one NUL terminator
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x00"

    return buf

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR() uses in crm_log_output_fn stub.
# The stub requests four strings (file, function, prefix, output) and two unsigned ints.
# Fuzzer infra will split this buffer; we just need to provide an initial valid buffer
# that likely yields meaningful values for those parameters when interpreted as strings.
#
# Assumptions about harness:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR() pulls a length-prefixed or NUL-terminated slice from the buffer.
# - We can maximize usefulness by including multiple NUL-terminated strings with
#   realistic content and varied lengths, followed by some bytes for integers.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit 4 NUL-terminated UTF-8 strings in order: file path, function name, prefix, output text.
# - Keep within fuzzer-imposed max truncations: file/function/prefix <= 256, output <= 1024.
# - Provide diverse characters: alnum, path separators, dots, underscores, hyphens, spaces.
# - For output text, include multiple lines to exercise line-splitting behavior.
# - Append 8 bytes of little-endian unsigned integers to cover line and level variety.
# - Total size capped under 4096 bytes.

PATH_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "/._-"
IDENT_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
PREFIX_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_ -[]#:/"
TEXT_CHARS = string.printable.replace("\x0b", " ").replace("\x0c", " ")

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, s: str, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(s) for _ in range(n))

def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create plausible paths with directories and extension
    roots = ["/var/log", "/tmp", "/home/user", ".", "..", "/etc/pacemaker", "/var/lib/pacemaker"]
    exts = [".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".hpp", ".log", ".txt", ".xml"]
    root = rng.choice(roots)
    parts = [root]
    # 1-3 components
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, PATH_CHARS.strip("/"), rng.randint(3, 12)))
    leaf_base = _rand_choice(rng, string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-", rng.randint(3, 12))
    ext = rng.choice(exts)
    parts.append(leaf_base + ext)
    path = "/".join(p.strip("/") for p in parts if p)
    if path.startswith("//"):
        path = path.lstrip("/")
    return path[:256]

def _make_function(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # C-like identifier with optional namespace-like prefixes
    prefixes = ["pcmk_", "crm_", "stonith_", "services_", "resources_", "main", "do_", "log_"]
    base = rng.choice(prefixes)
    tail = _rand_choice(rng, IDENT_CHARS, rng.randint(3, 20))
    return (base + tail)[:256]

def _make_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Logging prefix often includes level words, tags, pid, etc.
    levels = ["DEBUG", "INFO", "NOTICE", "WARN", "ERROR", "CRIT"]
    tag = _rand_choice(rng, IDENT_CHARS, rng.randint(3, 10))
    pid = str(rng.randint(1, 65535))
    fmt = rng.choice([
        f"[{rng.choice(levels)}] {tag}({pid}): ",
        f"{rng.choice(levels)} {tag}: ",
        f"{tag}: ",
        f"",
    ])
    # Add small random suffix decorations
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        fmt += _rand_choice(rng, PREFIX_CHARS, rng.randint(0, 8))
    return fmt[:256]

def _make_output_text(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Multi-line text to exercise line-by-line logging, include XML-ish and paths.
    lines: List[str] = []
    # 3-10 lines
    n = rng.randint(3, 10)
    for i in range(n):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            # XML-like snippet
            key = _rand_choice(rng, IDENT_CHARS, rng.randint(3, 10))
            val = _rand_choice(rng, TEXT_CHARS.replace("\n", ""), rng.randint(3, 20)).strip()
            lines.append(f"<{key}>{val}</{key}>")
        elif choice < 0.4:
            # Key=Value
            k = _rand_choice(rng, IDENT_CHARS, rng.randint(3, 12))
            v = _rand_choice(rng, TEXT_CHARS.replace("\n", ""), rng.randint(0, 30)).strip()
            lines.append(f"{k}={v}")
        elif choice < 0.6:
            # Path and message
            lines.append(f"path={_make_filename(rng)} msg={_rand_choice(rng, TEXT_CHARS, rng.randint(5, 40)).strip()}")
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # Plain sentence
            lines.append(_rand_choice(rng, TEXT_CHARS, rng.randint(10, 60)).strip())
        else:
            # Mixed unicode-like ASCII plus brackets
            lines.append(f"[{i}] {_rand_choice(rng, TEXT_CHARS, rng.randint(5, 50)).strip()}")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    return text[:1024]

def _u32_le(n: int) -> bytes:
    return n.to_bytes(4, byteorder="little", signed=False)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    file_s = _make_filename(rng)
    func_s = _make_function(rng)
    prefix_s = _make_prefix(rng)
    out_s = _make_output_text(rng)

    # Two unsigned ints: line (0..99999) and level (0..255)
    line = rng.randint(0, 99999)
    level = rng.randint(0, 255)

    # Assemble as NUL-terminated strings followed by integers.
    parts = []
    for s in (file_s, func_s, prefix_s, out_s):
        parts.append(s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00")
    parts.append(_u32_le(line))
    parts.append(_u32_le(level))

    blob = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure cap
    return blob[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: function name string
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() four times to supply C strings for:
# - file (source filename string)
# - function (C function name)
# - prefix (log prefix)
# - output (multi-line text to log)
# It also uses FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) twice for line and level, which our
# generator cannot influence directly; we focus on producing interesting strings.
#
# Goal: Provide a bytes buffer that the harness will slice into multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations and produce valid, diverse, and interesting inputs.
# We craft a single buffer that concatenates multiple NUL-terminated strings
# in an order likely consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We include multiple
# sets so that if the harness draws more strings than expected, it still finds
# reasonable values.
#
# Strategy for strings:
# - file: typical filenames, absolute/relative, with extensions and paths
# - function: identifier-like names including namespaces and underscores
# - prefix: short tags, brackets, severity-like prefixes
# - output: multi-line text with various line lengths, UTF-8, tabs, long lines
# Ensure max overall size <= 4096 bytes.

IDENT_START = string.ascii_letters + "_"
IDENT_CONT = IDENT_START + string.digits


def rand_ident(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    n = r.randint(1, max_len)
    s = r.choice(IDENT_START)
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        s += r.choice(IDENT_CONT)
    return s


def rand_namespace_ident(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Sometimes C++-style namespaces or struct-qualified names
    choices = [
        lambda: rand_ident(r, 12),
        lambda: rand_ident(r, 10) + "::" + rand_ident(r, 12),
        lambda: rand_ident(r, 10) + ":" + rand_ident(r, 12),  # single colon too
        lambda: rand_ident(r, 8) + "_" + rand_ident(r, 16),
    ]
    return r.choice(choices)()


def rand_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    exts = [".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".hpp", ".py", ".go", ".txt", ".log"]
    parts: List[str] = []
    depth = r.choices([0, 1, 2, 3], weights=[2, 4, 3, 1])[0]
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(rand_ident(r, 8))
    base = rand_ident(r, 10)
    ext = r.choice(exts)
    path = "/".join(parts + [base + ext]) if parts else base + ext
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        path = "/" + path  # absolute path
    return path


def rand_prefix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    presets = [
        "", "[INFO] ", "[DEBUG] ", "[WARN] ", "[ERROR] ",
        "pcmk: ", "stonith: ", "crm: ",
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        return r.choice(presets)
    # random short token with delimiter
    tok = rand_ident(r, 8)
    return tok + ": "


def rand_line(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Include ASCII, spaces, tabs; occasionally some UTF-8.
    base_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -._,/:#()[]{}\t"
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = "".join(r.choice(base_chars) for _ in range(n))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        # sprinkle some UTF-8
        extras = ["π", "λ", "✓", "é", "ø", "—", "£", "©"]
        pos = r.randint(0, len(s))
        s = s[:pos] + r.choice(extras) + s[pos:]
    return s


def rand_output(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build multi-line output up to ~1KB typical, respecting the stub's 1024 cap.
    lines = []
    count = r.randint(3, 20)
    for i in range(count):
        if i == 0 and r.random() < 0.5:
            # First line sometimes looks like a header
            lines.append("==== Begin Log Output ====")
            continue
        # Mix short and long lines
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            lines.append("")
        else:
            max_len = r.choice([40, 80, 120, 200])
            lines.append(rand_line(r, 3, max_len))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append("==== End Log Output ====")
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    # Trim to reasonable size; fuzzer will cap to 1024 anyway.
    return text[:1200]


def build_c_string(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; then NUL-terminate.
    return s.replace("\x00", "").encode("utf-8", "replace") + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Prepare several sets to cover multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls robustly.
    sets = []
    num_sets = 3  # enough diversity while keeping under size limits
    for _ in range(num_sets):
        file_s = rand_filename(r)
        func_s = rand_namespace_ident(r)
        prefix_s = rand_prefix(r)
        out_s = rand_output(r)
        sets.append((file_s, func_s, prefix_s, out_s))

    # Interleave strings in the order they are likely requested by the stub:
    # file, function, prefix, output (and repeat for extra availability).
    buf = bytearray()
    for file_s, func_s, prefix_s, out_s in sets:
        for s in (file_s, func_s, prefix_s, out_s):
            chunk = build_c_string(s)
            # Ensure total stays <= 4096
            if len(buf) + len(chunk) > 4096:
                # if adding would exceed, stop adding more data
                break
            buf += chunk
        if len(buf) >= 4096:
            break

    # As a small bonus, append a few extra identifier-like strings in case the
    # harness consumes more FUZZ_PARAM_STR() than anticipated.
    if len(buf) < 4096:
        extras = [rand_ident(r, 16) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4))]
        for s in extras:
            chunk = build_c_string(s)
            if len(buf) + len(chunk) > 4096:
                break
            buf += chunk

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, include_newlines: bool = False) -> str:
    # Generate readable ASCII; optionally include newlines to exercise line-splitting
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    if include_newlines:
        # Add some newlines and tabs sparsely
        chars += "\n\t"
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure not empty unless explicitly allowed by min_len
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    return s

def _likely_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a plausible C source-like filename with optional path components
    exts = [".c", ".cpp", ".cc", ".h", ".hpp", ".py", ".go", ".txt", ""]
    parts = []
    depth = rng.choices([0,1,2], weights=[5,3,2], k=1)[0]
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8).replace('/', '_'))
    base = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12).replace('/', '_')
    ext = rng.choice(exts)
    name = base + ext
    if parts:
        return "/".join(parts + [name])
    return name

def _likely_function(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # C-like identifier
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + '_')
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_') for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 24)))
    return first + rest

def _log_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Short prefix with brackets/ids commonly seen in logs
    choices: List[str] = [
        "pacemaker:",
        "stonith:",
        "scheduler:",
        "crm:",
        "DEBUG:",
        "INFO:",
        "WARN:",
        "ERROR:",
    ]
    base = rng.choice(choices)
    # Occasionally add context tags
    extras = []
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        extras.append(f"node={_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        extras.append(f"tid={rng.randint(1, 9999)}")
    if extras:
        base += " [" + ",".join(extras) + "]"
    return base

def _log_output_body(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Multi-line output to exercise splitting; include various characters
    lines = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    for i in range(n):
        # Mix plain text with XML-ish and key=value formats
        style = rng.random()
        if style < 0.35:
            lines.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 10, 80))
        elif style < 0.7:
            # XML-like line
            tag = _likely_function(rng)
            attrk = _likely_function(rng)
            attrv = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12).replace('"', '')
            lines.append(f"<{tag} {attrk}=\"{attrv}\"/>")
        else:
            # key=value list
            pairs = [f"{_likely_function(rng)}={_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10).replace(' ', '_')}" for _ in range(rng.randint(2,5))]
            lines.append(" ".join(pairs))
    return "\n".join(lines)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build fields expected by the fuzzer stub in order: file, function, prefix, output, then two uint32 values for line and level
    file_s = _likely_filename(rng)
    func_s = _likely_function(rng)
    prefix_s = _log_prefix(rng)
    out_s = _log_output_body(rng)

    # Constrain approximate lengths to stay within stub truncation limits for variety
    if len(file_s) > 256:
        file_s = file_s[:256]
    if len(func_s) > 256:
        func_s = func_s[:256]
    if len(prefix_s) > 256:
        prefix_s = prefix_s[:256]
    if len(out_s) > 1024:
        out_s = out_s[:1024]

    # Create two 32-bit values: line (0..99999) and level (0..255)
    line = rng.randint(0, 99999)
    level = rng.randint(0, 255)

    # Serialize as simple length-prefixed strings followed by two uint32 in little-endian.
    # Format: [len32][file][len32][func][len32][prefix][len32][output][u32 line][u32 level]
    def pack_str(s: str) -> bytes:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > 2048:
            b = b[:2048]
        return len(b).to_bytes(4, 'little') + b

    buf = bytearray()
    buf += pack_str(file_s)
    buf += pack_str(func_s)
    buf += pack_str(prefix_s)
    buf += pack_str(out_s)
    buf += int(line).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False)
    buf += int(level).to_bytes(4, 'little', signed=False)

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: free-form text for logging fields (file, function, prefix, output)
# The stub pulls 4 FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values with max lengths: file<=256, func<=256,
# prefix<=256, output<=1024. It also uses two integers but those are generated by the fuzzer,
# not from our buffer. Our goal is to return bytes that the fuzzer will slice into
# multiple strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR. We therefore construct a buffer that encodes
# multiple interesting strings separated in a manner the harness expects (typically
# length-prefixed or NUL-separated). Since the stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR (common pattern
# is to read a length then bytes, or read until NUL), we emit a sequence of NUL-terminated
# strings to maximize compatibility. Each string is crafted to exercise different
# logging behaviors: simple names, paths, long lines, multi-line text, unicode, and
# edge cases (empty, only spaces, very long without newlines).

# We keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

def _rand_path(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name_len = r.randint(1, max(1, max_len // (depth + 1)))
        name_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
        name = ''.join(r.choice(name_chars) for _ in range(name_len))
        parts.append(name)
    return "/" + "/".join(parts)

def _rand_func(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 48) -> str:
    prefix = r.choice(["main", "worker", "process", "handle", "parse", "serialize", "compute"])  # common function prefixes
    suffix_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    suffix = ''.join(r.choice(suffix_chars) for _ in range(r.randint(0, max(0, max_len - len(prefix)))))
    return (prefix + suffix)[:max_len]

def _rand_prefix(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 64) -> str:
    variants = [
        "",  # empty -> no prefix
        "INFO:",
        "WARN:",
        "ERROR:",
        "DEBUG:",
        "TRACE:",
        "[cluster]",
        "(pacemaker)",
        "node-" + str(r.randint(1, 9999)),
    ]
    base = r.choice(variants)
    if base and r.random() < 0.5:
        base += " "
    if len(base) < max_len and r.random() < 0.3:
        # add tag
        tag = r.choice(["ra", "stonith", "cib", "pe", "lrmd", "crm"]) + ":"
        base = (tag + " " + base).strip()
    return base[:max_len]

def _make_multiline(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Compose multiple lines with varied content, including unicode and unusual whitespace
    lines: List[str] = []
    pools = [
        string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.",
        string.punctuation.replace("\x00", ""),
    ]
    # Include some known keywords
    keywords = [
        "start", "stop", "monitor", "status", "reboot", "on", "off",
        "resource=ip-1", "agent=ocf:pacemaker:Dummy", "exit=0",
    ]
    # Add a mixture of lines
    for i in range(r.randint(3, 10)):
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            line = r.choice(keywords)
        else:
            pool = r.choice(pools)
            ln = r.randint(5, 80)
            line = ''.join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(ln))
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            # add some unicode
            uni_choices = ["✓", "✗", "–", "—", "«»,", "αβγ", "日本語"]
            line += " " + r.choice(uni_choices).replace(",", "")
        lines.append(line)
    text = "\n".join(lines)
    # Optionally end with newline
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        text += "\n"
    return text[:target_len]

def _rand_output(r: random.Random, max_len: int = 1024) -> str:
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        return _make_multiline(r, max_len)
    elif choice < 0.5:
        # Long single line without newline
        pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " .:-/_[](){}@#"
        ln = r.randint(200, max(200, max_len))
        return ''.join(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(min(ln, max_len)))
    elif choice < 0.75:
        # Structured-like output
        items = []
        while True:
            k = r.choice(["time", "node", "rsc", "action", "rc", "status"]) 
            v = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
            items.append(f"{k}={v}")
            s = ' '.join(items)
            if len(s) > max_len - 16 or r.random() < 0.2:
                break
        return s[:max_len]
    else:
        # Include many newlines and indentation
        blocks = []
        for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
            hdr = r.choice(["Section", "Block", "Node", "Result"]) + ":"
            body = _make_multiline(r, max_len // 2)
            blocks.append(hdr + "\n    " + body.replace("\n", "\n    "))
        out = "\n\n".join(blocks)
        return out[:max_len]

def _nul_join(parts: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join parts with NUL terminators and ensure final NUL to delimit
    joined = "\x00".join(parts) + "\x00"
    return joined.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build the four strings expected by the stub
    file_s = r.choice([
        _rand_path(r, 128),
        "src/cluster/pe_utils.c",
        "lib/services/actions.c",
        "main.c",
        "../../fuzz/input.cc",
    ])
    # Occasionally supply an empty or relative name
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        file_s = r.choice(["", "./", ".", "./log.c"])
    file_s = file_s[:256]

    func_s = _rand_func(r, 256)
    # Sometimes use common C-style names
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        func_s = r.choice(["main", "init_logging", "pcmk_simulate", "crm_log_output", "process_event"])[:256]

    prefix_s = _rand_prefix(r, 256)

    out_s = _rand_output(r, 1024)

    parts = [file_s, func_s, prefix_s, out_s]

    blob = _nul_join(parts)
    # Ensure size <= 4096
    return blob[:4096]
